newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon BLOM bank strengthens leading position.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon BLOM bank strengthens leading position.

text.p: Banque du Liban et d'Outre Mer reported increases of 28.5 percent in net income, 68 percent in customer deposits and 61.3 percent in assets in 1996, the bank said in a statement issued on Thursday.
BLOM also doubled its shareholders' equity to $154 million from $77 million at the end of 1995, rising to second from fourth place among Lebanon's 82 banks in terms of capital.
Return on average assets edged up to 1.1 percent from 1.06 percent in 1995, the bank added.
"BLOM strengthened its leading position in terms of deposits, position held for the past 15 consecutive years, showing a 68 percent increase over 1995 figures to reach $2.702 billion," the bank said.
"Assets grew by 61.3 percent to $3.031 billion...Net income reached about $27 million," it added.

The statement was issued after the Paris-based a Al-Iktissad Wal-Aamal, a Lebanese weekly business magazine, issued a preliminary ranking of the country's top 18 banks -- placing BLOM first in terms of assets and deposits.
The ranking was based on the banks' unaudited 1996 results.
BLOM has 33 branches in Lebanon and one in Cyprus and has 840 employees, according to the Almanac of the Lebanese Banks Association.
